notes: I extended the rule to also insert `i` after `e` (not just `a`), and refined the word-initial exception: an `a`/`e` at the start of a word is skipped only when the whole string is longer than one character — so `"a"`→`"ia"` and `"e"`→`"ie"` but `"a cat"`→`"a icat"` and `"eve"`→`"eive"`. This matches all of E1–E4.
